body.h3: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled
body.text: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled

body.h3: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled
body.text: 6 December 2023

body.h3: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled
body.text: People identified as homeless in Census 2021 were twice as likely as the rest of the population to be disabled.

body.h3: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled
body.text: Of those identified as homeless on census day (meaning those who were in hostels or homeless shelters, but not those sleeping rough), 4 in 10 (44.1%) were disabled. This compares with 17.5% of people in the wider population.

body.h3: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled
body.text: People identified as homeless were also 8 years younger on average than the wider population. Females identified as homeless were on average 16 years younger than the rest of the female population.

body.h3: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled
body.text: People identified as homeless were more likely than the rest of the population to hold no formal qualifications and were also disproportionately likely to identify within “Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African”, “Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups”, or “Other ethnic group”.

body.h3: Around 4 in 10 people identified as homeless in 2021 were disabled

body.h3: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending
body.text: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending

body.h3: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending
body.text: 1 December 2023

body.h3: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending
body.text: Spending on debit cards in the UK, as measured by [Revolut](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/economicoutputandproductivity/output/datasets/revolutspendingondebitcards), rose by 9% in the week to 26 November, compared with the week before.

body.h3: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending
body.text: The largest increase was in “retail”, with spending up 17%. This is in line with expected Black Friday weekend and pre-Christmas spending patterns.

body.h3: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending
body.text: Total Revolut debit card spending is 6% higher than the level seen in the equivalent week in 2022. Five of the six spending sectors increased in this time, with ”food and drink” reporting the largest increase of 11%.

body.h3: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending
body.text: Spending in ”pubs, restaurants, and fast food” fell by 3% when compared with the equivalent week of 2022.

body.h3: Black Friday gives boost to retail spending

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: 4 December 2023

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: People with children and those living in rented accommodation are among groups more likely to report a range of impacts from cost-of-living pressures, such as running out of food.

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: Between 12 July and 1 October 2023, 8% of parents living with a dependent child reported running out of food and being unable to afford more, compared with 5% of adults overall. Among renters, 13% reported running out of food.

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: Among parents of dependent children who were also renters, one in five (21%) reported running out of food before they could afford to buy more.

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: Lone parents were also particularly likely to be affected: 61% of lone adults living with at least one dependent child reported difficulty affording their rent or mortgage payments, compared with 40% of all adults making such payments.

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: Difficulty affording rent and mortgage payments was also more common among Asian and Asian British adults (56%), and Black, African, Caribbean or Black British adults (51%).

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food
body.text: Around 3 in 10 adults (29%) said they would not be able to afford an unexpected expense of £850 or more. This rose to 40% of disabled adults and 53% of renters. Among disabled adults who were renters, two-thirds (66%) reported being unable to afford such an expense.

body.h3: Renters and parents more likely to report running out of food

body.h3: Large pay gaps remain between Black British and White employees
body.text: 29 November 2023

body.h3: Large pay gaps remain between Black British and White employees
body.text: Black, African, Caribbean or Black British workers consistently earned less than their White counterparts over an 11-year period.

body.h3: Large pay gaps remain between Black British and White employees
body.text: The Annual Population Survey revealed that between 2012 and 2022, White employees earned £14.35 per hour (median gross hourly pay), while Black, African, Caribbean or Black British workers earned £13.53 per hour – 82 pence less.

body.h3: Large pay gaps remain between Black British and White employees
body.text: Between 2012 and 2022, they were the only ethnicity group to consistently earn less than White employees.

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: 15 November 2023

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: The rate at which prices of goods and services are rising has fallen to the lowest level since November 2021, according to the [Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers’ housing costs (CPIH)](https://www.ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukoctober2023).

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: Annual CPIH inflation, rose by 4.7% in the year to October 2023, down from 6.3% in September.

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: CPIH inflation has fallen from a recent peak of 9.6% in October 2022, which was the highest in over 40 years according to [indicative estimates](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/inflationandpriceindices/articles/consumerpriceinflationhistoricalestimatesandrecenttrendsuk/1950to2022).

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: Some of the main downward effects on inflation came from housing and household services, particularly gas and electricity prices.

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: Gas prices fell 31.0% in the year to October 2023, while electricity prices fell by 15.6%. These are the lowest annual inflation rates for gas and electricity since records began in January 1989.

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years
body.text: Energy prices remain high, however. The price of gas in October 2023 was around 60% higher than two years previously, while the price of electricity was 40% higher.

body.h3: Inflation falls to lowest level in almost two years

body.h3: Real terms pay continues to rise as vacancies keep falling
body.text: Real terms pay continues to rise as vacancies keep falling

body.h3: Real terms pay continues to rise as vacancies keep falling
body.text: 14 November 2023

body.h3: Real terms pay continues to rise as vacancies keep falling
body.text: Annual pay growth in real terms (adjusted for inflation) across Great Britain rose on the year by 1.4% for total pay (including bonuses) and 1.3% for regular pay (excluding bonuses), respectively, according to the latest data from the UK Labour Market Survey.

body.h3: Real terms pay continues to rise as vacancies keep falling
body.text: By contrast, annual growth for regular pay (not adjusted for inflation) was 7.7% in July to September 2023. Though slightly lower than previous periods, this remains one of the highest annual growth rates since comparable records began in 2001.

body.h3: Real terms pay continues to rise as vacancies keep falling
body.text: Estimated UK job vacancies fell in August to October 2023 for the 16th consecutive period, dropping by 58,000 vacancies to 957,000 on the quarter. This represents a decrease of 5.7% since May to July 2023 across 16 of the 18 industry sectors.
